segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the last few lectures I've been talking about the history of domestic building construction.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But today I want to begin looking at some contemporary, experimental designs for housing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So,I'm going to start with a house which is constructed more or less under the ground.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And one of the interesting things about this project is that the owners - both professionals but not architects - wanted to be closely involved, so they decided to manage the project themselves.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Their chief aim was to create somewhere that was as environmentally-friendly as possible. [[ ]] But at the same time they wanted to live somewhere peaceful - they'd both grown up in a rural area and disliked urban life.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So the first thing they did was to look for a site.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And they found a disused stone quarry in a beautiful area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The price was relatively low, [[ ]] and they liked the idea of recycling the land, as it were.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As it was, the quarry was an ugly blot on the landscape, and it wasn't productive any longer, either.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They consulted various architects and looked at a number of designs before finally deciding on one.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As I've said, it was a design for a sort of underground house, and it was built into the earth itself, with two storeys.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The north, east and west sides were set in the earth, and only the sloping, south-facing side was exposed to light.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That was made of a double layer of very strong glass. [[ ]] There were also photovoltaic tiles fixed to the top and bottom of this sloping wall.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These are tiles that are designed to store energy from the sun.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And the walls had a layer of foam around them too, to increase the insulation. [[ ]] Now, what is of interest to us about this project is the features which make the building energy-efficient.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Sunlight floods in through the glass wall, and to maximise it there are lots of mirrors and windows inside the house. [[ ]] That helps to spread the light around.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So that's the first thing - light is utilised as fully as possible.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In addition, the special tiles on the outside convert energy from the sun and generate some of the house's electricity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In fact, and it's possible that in future the house may even generate an electricity surplus, [[ ]] and that the owners will be able to sell some to the national grid.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As well as that, wherever possible, recycled materials have been used.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For example, the floors are made of reclaimed wood. [[ ]] And the owners haven't bought a single item of new furniture - they just kept what they already had.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And then there's the system for dealing with the waste produced in the house.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This is dealt with organically [[ ]] - it's purified by being filtered through reed beds which have been planted for that purpose in the garden.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So the occupants of the house won't pollute the land or use any damaging chemicals.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's true that the actual construction of the house was harmful to the environment, mainly because they had to use massive amounts of concrete [[ ]] - one of the biggest sources of carbon dioxide in manufacturing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And, as you know, this is very damaging to the environment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In total, the house construction has released 70 tons of carbon dioxide into the air.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now that's a frightening thought.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, once the initial 'debt' has been cleared - and it’s been calculated that this will only take fifteen years [[ ]] - this underground house won’t cost anything - environmentally I mean - because unlike ordinary houses, it is run in a way that is completely environmentally friendly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, eco-housing like this is likely to become much more...
